newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE DOLLAR ENDS SOFTER ON IMPORT PRESSURE.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE DOLLAR ENDS SOFTER ON IMPORT PRESSURE.

text.p: The Zimbabwe dollar was quoted weaker against hard units at the close of Wednesday interbank trade, pushed down by importer demand which outweighed export receipts, dealers said.

"The dollar went down on the back of import pressure. There were a number of payments that had to be made but there are no longer that many receipts coming in now with the tobacco sales drawing to a close," one dealer said.
The local unit finished the day at 10.3400/3600 against the U.S. dollar from late Tuesday's 10.3150/3350 and was also quoted easier against pound sterling at 16.1930/2340 compared to 16.1300/1700.
It was at 6.7810/7960 from 6.7630/7790 versus the mark and at 2.2930/2990 against the rand, down from 2.2710/2770 at the close of the previous session.
